title: Harbor Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Harbor Health onboarding to Redwood. Agreed to run initial benchmark on representative request patterns and schedule security review next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (CSM), Priya (SE); Carlos (CTO), Aisha (Head of Data), Liam (DevOps), Maya Park (PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on onboarding plan, infra choices, security needs, and pilot success metrics. Action items captured at end.

00:00 - 00:28 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, joined by Jonah and Priya from our CS and SE teams. Carlos: you want to kick off with intros?
00:29 - 01:05 Carlos (CTO): Yeah thanks Maya. I'm Carlos, CTO at Harbor. We've got Aisha who owns the data side, Liam for infra, and Maya Park is PM. We're looking to get Redwood into production for chat summarization and triage routing, goal is reduce manual triage by 40%.
01:06 - 01:32 Jonah (CSM): Great, high level we'll run a short pilot then iterate; want to cover timeline, who does what, security. Quick question on timeline expectations from your side?
01:33 - 02:05 Maya Park (PM): Ideally pilot in 3-4 weeks, production in Q1. But security signoff is big for us so that might push.
02:06 - 02:40 Aisha (Head of Data): Also we need to be mindful of PHI; some messages could have identifiers. We need KMS and audit logging, and retention policies that align with our compliance team.
02:41 - 03:10 Priya (SE): Yep understood. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (HSM or cloud KMS) in Private deployments and Dedicated can integrate with KMS as well. We can share the KMS integration doc after the call.
03:11 - 04:00 Carlos (CTO): Quick architecture question — do you recommend hosted (fastest) or Dedicated/VPC for us? We have HIPAA constraints and need audit logs and network isolation.
04:01 - 04:40 Priya (SE): For strict HIPAA and VPC peering, our Private deployment (customer VPC with our control plane) or Dedicated in a VPC are the two choices. Hosted can be used with BAA in some cases but it's more complicated for PHI; we'll outline pros/cons in the runbook.
04:41 - 05:12 Liam (DevOps): For VPC peering, what's the standard network flow? Do you require inbound rules? Are services pulling or pushing?
05:13 - 05:48 Priya (SE): We typically require outbound peering from customer's VPC to Redwood endpoints; you can terminate in your VPC for private deployments. We'll include network diagram. Also note we can do client-side TLS and mutual TLS if needed.
05:49 - 06:30 Jonah (CSM): Re: audit logs, we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns and route logs; for compliance we can give export of request logs and structured traces. We'll pass our SOC2 artifacts in the next step.
06:31 - 07:10 Aisha (Head of Data): Good. Also curious about data retention defaults and ability to turn off retention for training.
07:11 - 07:40 Priya (SE): By default hosted retention is short, but for Private/Dedicated you control retention; we also have an option to disable usage retention for models. We'll send docs.
07:41 - 08:20 Maya (AE): Let's talk pilot scope — what are the priority routes? Carlos, I think you mentioned triage and summarization?
08:21 - 09:05 Carlos (CTO): Yes, route one is nurse messages triage, route two is patient message summarization for care team, route three is some categorization for routing. We'll share token estimates.
09:06 - 09:30 Aisha (Head of Data): Token distribution is spiky; some messages are long. We'll provide a sample distribution and 95th percentile lengths.
09:31 - 10:20 Priya (SE): That helps for batching and KV cache decisions; for long sequences we recommend models and quantization profiles tuned for cost. We'll propose a model profile in the benchmark.
10:21 - 11:00 Liam (DevOps): On infra—do you support autoscaling for Dedicated? We expect bursts during business hours.
11:01 - 11:45 Priya (SE): Yes Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You can set min/max GPU pools. We'll include example policies and expected cold-start behavior.
11:46 - 12:30 Jonah (CSM): One common question — latency vs cost tradeoff, what's your recommendation for triage (latency-sensitive) vs batch summarization (cost-sensitive)?
12:31 - 13:10 Priya (SE): Triage should be on lower-latency routes; choose a smaller model variant pinned with strict SLOs and prefer warm pools and caching. Summarization can use batching and higher compression/quantization to save cost. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
13:11 - 14:00 Carlos (CTO): For benchmarks, do you need production traffic or a sample? We can't send PHI raw.
14:01 - 14:45 Aisha (Head of Data): We can anonymize messages and give representative token lengths and a sampling of route weights. We'll produce a small synthetic dataset that mirrors distribution.
14:46 - 15:30 Priya (SE): That's perfect. SE will run a dedicated vs hosted benchmark with that synthetic data and produce latency/cost per 1k tokens and per-route p95.
15:31 - 16:10 Maya (AE): Timing — SE benchmark by week from today? Can we aim for results within 7 business days?
16:11 - 16:40 Priya (SE): Yes assuming we get the sample by Friday, I can run tests and share results by next Wednesday.
16:41 - 17:20 Liam (DevOps): Network questions: do you support VPC peering to AWS only or GCP as well? We run multi-cloud but primary is AWS.
17:21 - 18:05 Priya (SE): We support AWS VPC peering; GCP peering is supported for Private deployments as well but has different setup. We'll follow up with infra runbook specifics per cloud.
18:06 - 19:00 Jonah (CSM): Security review — we'll need to run a deeper session. Who should be on that? Recommend including your security engineer and our security/compliance lead.
19:01 - 19:40 Carlos (CTO): Yes, include our security lead, and legal for BAA.
19:41 - 20:30 Jonah (CSM): I'll share SOC2/ISO docs and propose a security deep dive on 2026-11-17. Does that work?
20:31 - 21:05 Aisha (Head of Data): Works for us.
21:06 - 21:45 Maya (AE): Ok next, integrations — what SDKs and tooling do you expect us to use?
21:46 - 22:20 Priya (SE): We have REST and SDKs (Python/Node). For production we recommend server-side SDK with retry/backoff and streaming for summarization. We'll share code snippets.
22:21 - 23:00 Liam (DevOps): Any terraform modules for infra?
23:01 - 23:40 Priya (SE): We have example terraform scripts for VPC peering and policy. We'll include that repo link in the runbook.
23:41 - 24:30 Carlos (CTO): Regarding rollouts, do you support canary/A-B and automatic fallback to other model variants?
24:31 - 25:10 Priya (SE): Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to a compatible variant. We'll show UI in the demo.
25:11 - 26:00 Aisha (Head of Data): Monitoring—what metrics will we get out of the box?
26:01 - 26:40 Jonah (CSM): Token-level cost, per-route latency, error rates, model version traces, and prompt/response sampling. We can also export traces to your observability stack.
26:41 - 27:20 Maya Park (PM): For success criteria — what are we defining for pilot pass? Carlos?
27:21 - 27:50 Carlos (CTO): Pilot pass = 40% reduction in manual triage time, p95 latency for triage routes < 350ms, and security signoff. If those are met we move to Dedicated in Q1.
27:51 - 28:30 Priya (SE): We'll target p95 numbers in the benchmark and propose config for warm pools and batching to meet latency.
28:31 - 29:15 Maya (AE): Ok commercial — will you need pricing up front or after benchmark? We can give an estimate and then firm numbers for Dedicated.
29:16 - 30:00 Carlos (CTO): An estimate is good. We need to budget for Q1.
30:01 - 30:45 Maya (AE): We'll send a cost estimate for pilot (hosted run) and high-level Dedicated sizing for planning.
30:46 - 31:30 Liam (DevOps): Any compliance controls around logs access/roles? We need RBAC and SSO (SAML) support.
31:31 - 32:10 Jonah (CSM): Yes SSO via SAML and RBAC are supported; we'll include role templates (admin, viewer, developer). We'll also note audit log retention options.
32:11 - 33:00 Aisha (Head of Data): One more – can we disable model training on usage data? We need an explicit opt-out and confirmation for PHI.
33:01 - 33:40 Priya (SE): Yes, we have an opt-out & retention control. For Private/Dedicated you control training data; hosted has a setting to disable usage for training. We'll document it.
33:41 - 34:20 Carlos (CTO): Great. Anything else on technical constraints?
34:21 - 35:00 Maya Park (PM): We'll need a one-page onboarding plan for our internal stakeholders.
35:01 - 35:40 Maya (AE): We'll provide a one-page runbook and a timeline.
35:41 - 36:20 Priya (SE): I'll include network diagram, terraform link, and sample benchmark config.
36:21 - 37:00 Jonah (CSM): I'll attach SOC2 artifacts and propose security deep-dive invite.
37:01 - 37:40 Carlos (CTO): Sounds good. Who's the point person from Redwood for day-to-day?
37:41 - 38:10 Maya (AE): Jonah will be your CSM and day-to-day contact, Priya is SE for technical stuff.
38:11 - 38:50 Liam (DevOps): For the benchmark, can we get some visibility into the exact model variants you'll test? We want to know hardware assumptions.
38:51 - 39:30 Priya (SE): We'll list model variants and quantization profiles; benchmarks will include GPU type and memory assumptions. We'll also show per-token cost estimates.
39:31 - 40:10 Aisha (Head of Data): Timeline recap?
40:11 - 40:40 Maya (AE): Action items and deliverables: runbook by 2026-11-11, VPC details by 2026-11-12, sample data by 2026-11-13, security review 2026-11-17, SE benchmark by 2026-11-18.
40:41 - 41:20 Carlos (CTO): Confirmed.
41:21 - 42:00 Maya Park (PM): We'll send calendar invites for the security call.
42:01 - 42:40 Jonah (CSM): I'll share the SOC2 bundle right after this call.
42:41 - 43:20 Maya (AE): Any final questions?
43:21 - 44:00 Liam (DevOps): Just one—what does support look like during pilot?
44:01 - 44:40 Jonah (CSM): We provide Slack support and a named CSM; for Dedicated there's 24/7 on-call options if needed. We'll detail this in the onboarding doc.
44:41 - 45:30 Carlos (CTO): Ok thanks everyone, excited to get started.
45:31 - 46:10 Maya (AE): Thanks all, we'll follow up with the checklist and send the next steps.
46:11 - 46:40 (Recording ends, wrap-up chatter, small talk)
